summary: @yudzxml/baileys 7.4.0 — Baileys fork; static keyword co-occurrence in messages-media.js requires human review
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library. a static rule matched on keyword co-occurrence in lib/Utils/messages-media.js: `require('child_process')`, `require('os')`, `require('http')`/`require('https')`, and `POST`/`GET`/`fetch(` calls, with the only cited literal URL being `https://mmg.whatsapp.net` (WhatsApp's own media server, which is the expected destination for a Baileys media utility). The evidence quotes do not name any non-first-party attacker endpoint, do not show environment-variable scraping, and do not show reads of installer-secret paths (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.npmrc`, browser stores). The primitive co-occurrence in messages-media.js is the shape you would expect from a legitimate WhatsApp media upload/download implementation (child_process for ffmpeg/thumbnail generation, http/https/fetch for WhatsApp media endpoints, os for tmpdir). Because this is a fork of a widely used upstream library, and forks are a common vehicle for covert modifications (e.g., undocumented actions using the caller's WhatsApp session), a reviewer should diff this fork against upstream Baileys to confirm messages-media.js only talks to `mmg.whatsapp.net`/WhatsApp infrastructure, and that no other file in the package performs credential harvest, undocumented auto-follow/subscribe, or exfiltration using the caller's session. Without corroborating evidence of installer harm, keyword co-occurrence alone is not sufficient to publish a block.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
